findings.description: No test pins a legitimate `ssh://host/`-form prefix match, or the rejection of a plausible path character outside `[A-Za-z0-9._/-]`. The `/` prefix is only exercised with local paths. If the charset were narrowed, for example by dropping `.` or `-`, `org/my-repo.git` over ssh would stop probing and no test would fail. A test listing `ssh://git@example.invalid/` and pushing to `ssh://git@example.invalid/org/my-repo_1.git` would pin it.

The new clause ", followed only by letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `/` and `-`," comes after the scp-form parenthetical, so it seems to qualify only that last item, or the whole list including whole-URL entries. The code (push_gate.rs L698-706) checks it only for prefix entries. Moving it into the prefix items would fix that, e.g. "where a prefix matches only when the rest of the URL is letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `/` and `-`".

The allowed set includes `/`, so the text after an scp-form prefix can start with `//`. Say the user lists an scp alias spelt like a built-in scheme (`git:`, `ssh:`, `http:`, `https:`, `file:`). Then a URL such as `git://evil.example/x` matches that entry and the probe connects to evil.example. The `!entry.contains("://")` guard checks only the entry, never the joined URL. The old `starts_with` allowed the same thing. A possible fix: refuse a match when the text after a `:` entry starts with `//`.
